clue.text: Black taxi in Hackney, say

indicators.note: one thing placed in another means the first word's letters sit inside the second's

blocks.note: a hackney is a breed of horse, and a mare is one kind of horse, so 'say' marks an example
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A black London cab out on the streets of Hackney, an East London borough.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney looks like the London borough a black cab drives through; here it is a breed of horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Black humour is grim, gruesome comedy, and macabre describes exactly that dark, death-obsessed quality.

clue.text: Reptilian old fogey on the radio?

definitions.note: adjective clueing a noun: a croc is a reptilian creature

indicators.note: something heard on the radio is only heard, so we go by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: an old crock is a worn-out, decrepit old person

explanation.surface: A cold-blooded old bore holding forth on a radio programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A croc is the short informal name for a crocodile, which is a large reptile.

clue.text: Antipodean, also in French and English

blocks.note: aussi is the French word for also
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone from Down Under who speaks French as well as English.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antipodes means Australia and New Zealand, and an Aussie is an Australian, a native of that region.

clue.text: Observation of suspect starter in savoury meal to go

indicators.note: a starter comes at the beginning, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: the first letter of savoury
a takeout is a meal bought to eat elsewhere, food to go

explanation.surface: Detectives watching a suspect order a savoury starter as a takeaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A stakeout is a police surveillance operation, keeping a watch on a suspect or place for some time.

clue.text: Back away, bird having escaped?

blocks.note: a chicken is a bird
an escaped animal is out of its pen

explanation.surface: Someone retreats from a fight, like a hen that has got loose from the coop.
explanation.definitionFit: To chicken out is to withdraw from something through fear, which is a cowardly retreat.

clue.text: A record maintained in vote against similar relationship, explained

indicators.note: something maintained in a thing is held within it, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
nay is a vote against, as in ayes and nays
a log is a record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: A record kept of a no vote, set against a comparable case.
explanation.walkthrough: Nay is the parliamentary word for a vote against, as in 'the ayes and the nays'.
explanation.definitionFit: An analogy explains something by comparing it with a parallel case, drawing out a likeness between two things.

clue.text: Helmet worn by Irish copper — style!

indicators.note: a hat worn by someone sits around them, so the helmet goes outside the other pieces

blocks.note: a helmet is a kind of hat
IR is an abbreviation for Irish
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: An Irish policeman in his helmet makes a fashion statement.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a policeman in a helmet, but it is the metal, symbol Cu. HA(IR CU)T.
explanation.definitionFit: A haircut is the style in which a person's hair is cut and shaped.

clue.text: Work of art that’s beautiful, though first scratched?

indicators.note: scratched means struck out, and first says it is the opening letter that goes

blocks.note: fetching means attractive or beautiful

explanation.surface: A lovely print that was made by scratching into a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: FETCHING loses its F. The surface is apt, since an etching is made by scratching lines into a metal plate.
explanation.definitionFit: An etching is a print made from a plate whose design was cut by acid, a recognised form of artwork.

clue.text: Session with nothing for defenceless individual

blocks.note: a sitting is a session, as of a court or a portrait painter
in cricket a duck is a score of nothing

explanation.surface: A meeting that achieves nothing to help the vulnerable.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a batsman's score of zero in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting duck is an easy target, someone exposed to attack and unable to protect themselves.

clue.text: Thin piece of wood put alongside similar piece?

definitions.text: Thin piece of wood put alongside similar piece?

indicators.note: put alongside means placed next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: a match is a thin piece of wood too, so it is a similar piece
a stick is a thin piece of wood

explanation.surface: A sliver of timber is laid next to another like it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a stick set next to a match describes the answer, and the question mark flags the double duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchstick is the slender wooden shaft of a match, literally a stick joined to a match head.

clue.text: Drink some sentimental octogenarian knocked over

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them
something knocked over is upended, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A soppy old person in their eighties spills a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cola is a sweet fizzy soft drink flavoured with kola nut.

clue.text: Hope for power in cult

indicators.note: one thing placed in another means its letters go inside the other word

blocks.note: pro means in favour of, for
P is the symbol for power in physics
a sect is a cult or religious faction

explanation.surface: A wish for influence within a religious cult.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the power sits inside the cult; 'for' stays in front as a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a possibility or expectation of something in the future, much like a hope.

clue.text: One of those active during strenuous exercise was tangled in knots

definitions.text: One of those active during strenuous exercise

indicators.note: something in knots is twisted and tangled up, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone working out hard got tied up in knots.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweat glands in the skin secrete perspiration, so they work hardest when the body is exerted in a workout.

clue.text: Anxious, personal pride about office having backfired

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other
something that has backfired has gone the wrong way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: ego is a sense of self-importance or personal pride
a den is a private room for work, a study or office

explanation.surface: A nervous person whose self-importance at work has come back to bite them.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on edge is an idiom meaning tense, nervous or jumpy.

clue.text: Where one goes to India, sent abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered, so the letters are dispersed and rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone posted overseas heads off to India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where one goes to' reads naturally as a phrase, but 'to' belongs with the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A destination is the place a person is travelling toward, the end point of a journey.

clue.text: All in Detroit upset about unemployment, primarily

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the letters are put in a new order
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is wanted
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the next piece

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
the first letter of unemployment

explanation.surface: Workers in Detroit, the US car-making city, are exhausted and distressed by joblessness.
explanation.walkthrough: All in is British slang for exhausted, not a gambling term here.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all in means completely worn out, just as tired out means utterly exhausted.

clue.text: Musician, 24 Down supposedly?

blocks.note: first meaning: a violinist, especially in folk music
second meaning: Nero is said to have fiddled while Rome burned

explanation.surface: Was the emperor at 24 Down really a performer?
explanation.walkthrough: 24 Down is NERO; the legend that he played the fiddle while Rome burned is doubtful, hence 'supposedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddler plays the violin, and legend casts the Roman emperor as one who played while his city went up in flames.

clue.text: Biscuit that’s alcoholic?

definitions.note: adjective clueing a noun: bourbon is an alcoholic drink

blocks.note: first meaning: a British chocolate sandwich biscuit with a chocolate cream filling
second meaning: an American whiskey distilled mainly from corn

explanation.surface: Is there booze in this biscuit?
explanation.walkthrough: A bourbon is a familiar British biscuit: two oblong chocolate biscuits with chocolate cream between.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name covers a chocolate cream biscuit in Britain and a corn whiskey from Kentucky.

clue.text: Drink with a horrid taste?

blocks.note: first meaning: a British style of draught beer, strongly hopped
second meaning: sharp and unpleasant on the tongue

explanation.surface: A drink that tastes awful.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain bitter is a type of pale beer served in pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an English ale and also the sharp, acrid flavour of things like strong coffee or quinine.

clue.text: Complete race for some charity

blocks.note: to do a task is to complete it
a nation is a people or race

explanation.surface: Finishing a sponsored run to raise money for a good cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is a gift of money, and charity in this sense means alms given to those in need.

clue.text: Caught, felon ultimately suffered

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is wanted

blocks.note: the final letter of felon
ailed means was unwell, suffered

explanation.surface: A criminal is arrested and eventually pays the price.
explanation.definitionFit: Nailed is informal for caught or arrested, as when police finally pin a culprit down.

clue.text: Great actor resting, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: judging by sound means the word is heard, not read, so spelling can change

blocks.note: idle means inactive or resting; actors call being out of work resting

explanation.surface: A celebrated star between jobs, which actors politely call resting.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a much-admired celebrity, a star worshipped by fans, which suits a great actor.

clue.text: Reference that’s indicatory, with arrangement of letters?

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things into a fresh order, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A reference book that points the way, its letters set in order.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, a dictionary is itself an arrangement of letters, alphabetically ordered words.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary is a reference book listing words with their meanings.

clue.text: Emperor certainly not impressing queen

indicators.note: impressing means pressing into, so the second piece is held within the first

blocks.note: no is a firm refusal
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: An emperor fails to win over the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was a Roman ruler of the first century AD, one of the most notorious of the Caesars.

clue.text: Shocking in-house reforms

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are reshaped into a new word

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange, hyphen ignored

explanation.surface: Internal company changes cause outrage.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinous means wicked or atrocious, so outrageous that it appals people.

clue.text: Space where Othello, for example, returned on stage

indicators.note: returned means sent back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
Shakespeare's Othello is the Moor of Venice

explanation.surface: An actor playing Othello comes back on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' suggests a theatre with Othello on it, but it is a leg of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Legroom is the space available for a seated person's legs, as in a car or aircraft.
